claims.text: Integrating high-resolution MDSC, advanced baseline correction, and simultaneous thermal-analysis cross-calibration will accurately and efficiently determine melting and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties in single-phase high-entropy alloys.
Al0.5CoCrFeNi is an example of an equiatomic high-entropy alloy.
The relevant Al0.5CoCrFeNi material is single-phase.
The specified single-phase alloys exhibit fcc or bcc phase structures.
The method is intended to operate from ambient temperature to approximately 1000–1600 °C under inert atmospheres and controlled heating and cooling rates.
Modulated thermal signals can distinguish reversing baseline heat-capacity contributions from non-reversing latent-heat contributions.
Subtle shifts in thermal-expansion behavior measured by the proposed setup indicate volume changes at melting.
Deconvolution of reversing and non-reversing MDSC components isolates the latent heat associated with fusion enthalpy.
Melting produces latent heat release.
MDSC baseline shifts directly reflect entropy changes during melting.
MDSC baseline shifts reflect volume expansion during melting.
The integrated method will determine melting temperature within ±3 K.
The integrated method will measure fusion enthalpy within ±5% accuracy.
The integrated method will measure fusion entropy within ±5% accuracy.
The integrated method can detect subtle volume changes at melting through calibrated baseline shifts.
Standard DSC has already been applied to high-entropy alloys.
Improved modulation and calibration can address high-temperature DSC measurement uncertainties.
The approach is applicable across single-phase high-entropy alloys.
Uncorrected calibration drift at extreme temperatures can reduce the method's accuracy.
Disagreement with the comparison method exceeding 3 K for melting temperature or 5% for fusion enthalpy or entropy would falsify the proposed performance claim.

contradictions.description: The alloy is called equiatomic, but Al0.5CoCrFeNi specifies half as much Al as each of Co, Cr, Fe, and Ni; normalized values are approximately Al 11.1 at.% and 22.2 at.% for each other element.

Simultaneous thermal analysis is described as an integrated cross-calibration module in the intervention but as an independent comparison technique in the falsification experiment, leaving its independence unclear.
